classification.difficultyReason: Part b links an exterior angle to two equal base angles, then uses a right-triangle angle sum and a supplementary angle; the other parts use shorter familiar chains.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ in the diagrams below, and explain your reasoning.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with all three internal angles labelled alpha and no side ticks.
Triangle with two beta base angles, perpendicular Bx extended above B, and AB extended above B. Lowercase x is a point label.
spec.mathematics: Exterior angle at B is 160 degrees; gamma is the left angle between the upward perpendicular and BA.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}2\beta&=160^\circ\\\beta&=80^\circ\end{align*}$

Exterior angle of $\triangle ABC$.

$\angle ABx=180^\circ-90^\circ-80^\circ=10^\circ$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABx$).

$\begin{align*}\gamma+10^\circ&=180^\circ\\\gamma&=170^\circ\end{align*}$

Adjacent angles on the straight line through $B$ and $x$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC, AC extended to D, and AE parallel to BC with matching arrow marks.
spec.mathematics: EAB=85 degrees, BCD=155 degrees, beta=ABC and gamma=BAC.

answer.worked:
$\beta=85^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AE\parallel BC$).

$\begin{align*}\gamma+85^\circ&=155^\circ\\\gamma&=70^\circ\end{align*}$

Exterior angle of $\triangle ABC$.
